experiment_name: Resume 027's frozen 32-game PURE PPO (hybrid=False) checkpoint for 96 additional games (128 total), then strength-test the 128-game candidate against the frozen 32-game checkpoint, 20 DEV seeds x 4 focus-seat rotation, deterministic masked-argmax

algorithm_config.purpose: 027's 32-game pure-PPO checkpoint was found stronger than its own untrained init (028, GO). Does continuing training on the SAME recipe (same PPOAgent/hybrid=False/hyperparameters/reward/action-space/state pipeline, reference train() unmodified) for 96 MORE games (128 total) add further real strength?
algorithm_config.algorithm_frozen: PPOAgent, ActorNetwork/architecture, PPO hyperparameters, reward shaping, action space, state pipeline, and the reference submodule were all identical to 027/028 - only the reference's own train()/PPOAgent.load/save were called, unmodified.

phase_1_resume_training.hash_gate: Both required to match before resuming - enforced via monopolyzero_pure_ppo_strength_screen.load_candidate_agent (reused unmodified), matched on the first attempt.
phase_1_resume_training.seed_derivation: train()'s own unmodified formula is episode_seed = seed_arg + absolute_game - 1, where absolute_game = games_trained_at_start + game_num (game_num 1..96). Choosing seed_arg=46968 (= 47000 - 32) makes the 96 episode seeds land exactly on 47000-47095 - verified at runtime by recomputing episode_seed for every logged game (log_every=1, all 96 entries) and asserting exact equality to the expected list; the script raises RuntimeError otherwise (would have stopped the run, not silently continued).
phase_1_resume_training.opponents: FPAgentA/FPAgentB/FPAgentC (reference monopoly_game_engine.agents_fixed, unmodified) - train()'s own hardcoded opponent pool, identical to 027
phase_1_resume_training.output_checkpoint_path: artifacts/monopolyzero_pure_ppo_learnability_gate/candidate_ppo_128.pt (SEPARATE file - the 32-game checkpoint was never overwritten, confirmed both files present with distinct SHA-256 after the run)
phase_1_resume_training.asu_involvement: none - reference train()/agent_ppo.py/networks.py grepped clean of asu in prior experiments (027), same call chain reused unmodified here; monopolyzero_common.loaded_asu_modules() also checked at runtime and returned empty

phase_2_strength_test.candidate: the 128-game checkpoint produced by phase 1 (used directly in-memory, no reload/re-verification against a separate hash - it was already hash-verified pre-resume and its own post-training games_trained==128 was asserted before proceeding)
phase_2_strength_test.baseline: 027's frozen 32-game checkpoint, reloaded fresh and hash-gated again (matched) via the same load_candidate_agent reuse
phase_2_strength_test.design: one CANDIDATE (128-game) focus seat + three identical copies of the BASELINE (32-game, frozen) per game, focus seat rotated across all 4 seats per seed
phase_2_strength_test.policy: deterministic legal-masked argmax for BOTH agents - reuses 028's build_masked_argmax_policy/play_one_game/summarize wholesale, unmodified (no new evaluation framework)
phase_2_strength_test.seed_pool: fresh DEV range 48000-48019, registered in scripts/evaluation_protocol.py before this run; disjoint from the training seeds (47000-47095) and from every prior experiment and FINAL_BLIND

pre_registered_decision_rule.primary_statistic: seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (128-game candidate win rate - 0.25), same evaluation_protocol.seed_block_bootstrap_vs_null used in 028
pre_registered_decision_rule.GO: lower bound of the CI is > 0
pre_registered_decision_rule.KILL: upper bound of the CI is <= 0
pre_registered_decision_rule.post_run_action: GO -> stop after reporting, no automatic scaling to 256/500/1000 games. KILL/INCONCLUSIVE -> also stop, no reward/architecture changes. Both paths are terminal for this task regardless of outcome.

result: INCONCLUSIVE per the pre-registered rule - the seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (128-game win rate - 25% null) is [-10.0, +11.25] points (point estimate exactly 0.0: candidate won 20/80 = 25.0%, landing exactly on the null itself), straddling zero. Neither GO (lower>0) nor KILL (upper<=0) is satisfied. 0 illegal actions, 0 crashes, 0 ASU modules loaded across all 176 games (96 training + 80 eval); episode seed range verified exactly 47000-47095 before any strength-test game ran. HOWEVER, a large, non-pre-registered behavioral finding must be reported alongside the flat win-rate result: continuing training from 32 to 128 games did NOT preserve or extend the 32-game checkpoint's dominant behavioral driver identified in 028 (BUY_PROPERTY chosen 98.5%-99.9% of legal opportunities in every prior pure-PPO measurement in this project). By 128 games, BUY_PROPERTY collapsed to EXACTLY 0.0% (0/3153 legal opportunities chosen) and ACCEPT_TRADE collapsed to 0.017% (5/30185) - meanwhile DECLINE_TRADE, which had been chosen 0% of the time in every prior experiment (027/028/029) despite being legal whenever ACCEPT_TRADE was, jumped to 27.5%. The frozen 32-game baseline retained its familiar 99.9% BUY_PROPERTY rate throughout this same run (playing the other three seats), confirming this is a real shift in the 128-game checkpoint's own policy, not a measurement artifact. Despite this dramatic behavioral collapse, the 128-game checkpoint still achieved a win rate statistically indistinguishable from the 32-game baseline (and from the 25% null) - net worth and bankruptcy both moved in the candidate's favor (mean net worth +1724.3, bankruptcy 20.0% vs. 45.4%), directionally positive but not part of the pre-registered primary statistic. This pattern reads as policy drift/instability under continued PPO training on this small-game-count recipe, not a confirmed improvement or a confirmed regression on the primary metric - it is a strong reason for caution before scaling this exact recipe further, independent of the INCONCLUSIVE win-rate verdict itself.
